prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: Brain activity was measured using functional near-infrared spectroscopy while participants took part in a 30-minute English class.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Anxiety levels were tracked through heart rate variability, and existing language skills were assessed using verbal fluency scores.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Learners with low anxiety displayed stronger connections within the brain's language network and learned more new words.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Learners with high anxiety showed a different pattern, suggesting that the specific brain areas for language were not engaged as effectively.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: For learners with high anxiety, stronger connections between the general demand network and the language network were linked to better learning, implying a compensatory role.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Learners with higher prior proficiency showed more distinct changes in the relationship between brain connectivity and performance depending on their anxiety level.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Learners with lower prior proficiency exhibited weaker and less flexible patterns in how their brain connectivity related to learning outcomes.
facts.subject: humans
